sentences.text:
S, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER 1.

Petitioner, who apprehends his arrest in Crime No.19/2024 registered by Kalasipalya Police Station, Bengaluru for the offences punishable under Sections 109, 120(B), 134, 406, 420, 465, 467,
468, 114, 417 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.19/2024 was registered by Kalasipalya Police Station, Bengaluru against one Das and others, for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 19.01.2024 received from Smt. Sasmitha Pangari, Senior Manager of Karnataka Bank, Minerva Circle Branch,
Bengaluru.
Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner had filed Crl.Misc.No.9934/2024 before the Jurisdictional Sessions Court which was rejected on 07.11.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner's name is not found in the FIR.
Accused No.2 has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.10669/2024 and accused No.3 has been granted regular bail by the jurisdictional Sessions Court.
The only allegation against the petitioner is that he had introduced accused Nos.1 to 3 to the Bank for the purpose of loan.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.

6. The material available on record would go to show that accused Nos.2 and 3 had borrowed a sum of Rs.62,99,000/- from the Karnataka Bank, Minerva Circle Branch, Bengaluru, in the year 2019 and since the accused borrowers had failed to repay the amount, loan account was treated as NPA in the year 2020 and subsequently, property which was the subject matter of the Sale Deed under which accused No.1 had sold the property in question in favour of accused No.2, was brought for sale by the Bank in the year 2022 itself.

The material on record would go to show that in the NC:
2024:KHC:51319 year 2022 itself, the Bank came to know about the alleged fraud played by accused Manjunath G vs State By Kalasipalya Police Station on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74991597/
2 persons, but first information is belatedly lodged after a period of two years.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, this Court has granted anticipatory bail to accused No.2 in Crl.P.No.10669/2024.
Petitioner's name is not found in the FIR.
The only allegation against him is that he had facilitated accused Nos.1 to 3 to borrow loan from the Bank.
Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.
Accordingly, the following order:-
7. The petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.19/2024 registered by Kalasipalya Police Station, Bengaluru for the offences punishable under Sections 109, 120(B), 134,
406, 420, 465, 467, 468, 114, 417 of IPC, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a NC: 2024:KHC:51319 personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
4. The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future.

SD/-
